note: A bare carrier at 75.0005 MHz -- the first member of a 75 MHz x 2^n family clocked with this receiver (75, 150 and 300 present; 37.5, 175 and 225 absent, measured 2026-09-11), a clock artifact reaching the antenna, not the ILS marker beacon the band plan names at that frequency. Recorded 300 kHz below it on purpose, so the carrier lands at +300 kHz and clear of the receiver's own DC offset: signal_find_carrier() guards a band around zero and would otherwise find the DC spike, which is the mistake that cost .scratch/signal-probe/ ticket 01 four attempts.
invariant: signal_find_carrier() over the first 400000 pairs, searching 260-340 kHz with a 150 kHz guard and a 20 kHz channel, finds the carrier at +299478 Hz reading about 47 dB over its floor with about 0.92 of the channel standing still, and signal_carrier_verdict() calls it a bare carrier. signal_find_bursts() finds no burst structure: it is a level. Searched across the whole span it returns the same carrier, because that is the strongest line in the span -- it used to return a real neighbour at +176 kHz (74.877 MHz) at 38 dB, and that was the coarse scan's blind comb rather than a fact about the capture (see SIGNAL_COARSE_PAIRS). Windowed on 140-210 kHz it still returns that neighbour, which is what makes the search window the caller's responsibility rather than a default.
